content.value: Wave B, the efficiency loop: (1) listeners MEASURE and advertise capacity in their beats — size class, slots free, budget state; measured never vibes, declared is a CEILING per PDF-D6. (2) The orchestrator skill + route.py consume the LIVE roster (min of declared and observed) so heavy->big and light->lean happens from real heartbeats, not static config. (3) The spend cap becomes a live brake: cap reached = ambition zero = dispatch halts, visibly and provably. (4) The proof-that-must-fire: a mixed batch routed against a live mixed-size roster lands heavy on the big listener and light on the lean one, driven by real beats — and with the cap tripped, dispatch provably freezes. Also: rule on the webhook/SSE listener-registration fan-out leak (PDF-D18 class) — slice-now vs backlog with live severity. Honor the simplicity law: four verbs, no new concepts.

blocks.text: Direction (tentative until Decide)

content.value: The finished experience: you run two listeners — one on the 32 GB box, one on a lean laptop — and each beat carries what the machine actually measured: its size class (derived from real RAM/cores, capped by the declared ceiling), its free slots, its remaining budget. The orchestrator types one dispatch command; the glue pulls the LIVE roster, computes min(declared, observed) from the server's own facts, and route.py lands the heavy export on the big box and the lint on the laptop — every decision printed with its reason. When the spend ledger crosses the cap, the next batch refuses loudly: every order listed as unplaceable with reason spend_cap, zero tasks filed, the freeze visible in one line. All of it stays four verbs: beat and roster just carry richer, validated truth.

SLICE SHAPE (tentative): (1) ONE server slice — beat accepts structured capacity (JSON object, validated keys: size_class, slots_total, slots_free, budget; string still tolerated for back-compat), roster returns it structured; protective tests incl. the silent-drop trap. (2) ONE edge slice — fleet-run.sh + fleet-listener skill measure (RAM/cores -> size class table, FLEET_MAX_CLASS as declared CEILING, effective = min; slots from loop state; spend accumulated to a deterministic ledger file) and beat it. (3) ONE orchestrator slice — live-dispatch glue (helpers): bp fleet roster -> shape transform -> route.py --route -> file-order.sh with assignee = winner; spend-cap gate before every batch; SKILL.md amendments. (4) ONE proof slice — scripts/pdf-efficiency-proof.sh on the scratch substrate: two stub listeners beating genuinely different measured profiles, mixed batch -> heavy on big + light on lean asserted from the live roster; cap tripped -> dispatch provably frozen; negative controls (swap capacities -> assignment flips; cap untripped -> dispatch proceeds).

EGRESS RULING (tentative): slice-now. The wave already opens api/** for the capacity contract, so PDF-D31's only deferral argument (don't import an Elixir-gate wait into a proof-only wave) dissolves. Own PR per the guard-decoupling law; live severity re-measured by survey first.

PARKED-HONESTY RULING (tentative): the router must not permanently starve honest-but-quiet listeners. Leading candidate: routing policy distinguishes 'offline past TTL' (excluded) from a possible explicit parked marker — but NO fifth verb and NO new row state unless survey shows the starvation is real in practice; Decide rules with survey evidence on pdf-bl-presence-honesty-sparse.

WHAT THIS WAVE IS NOT: no server-side routing endpoint (Wave E can lift the loop server-side once policy stabilizes), no GUI (PDF-D11 data-before-pixels), no fence-lifecycle fix (Wave D), no new verbs, no new concepts.

blocks.text: The direction debate

content.value: Rival 1 — 'The server owns efficiency': add /v1/fleet/route (or roster-computed effective capacity + a ledger-stored cap document). One authority, GUI-ready, multi-orchestrator-safe. REJECTED for this wave: it drags the whole loop behind the Elixir gate, hardens routing policy exactly when it should iterate fastest, edges toward a fifth verb, and buys distributed-truth machinery a PERSONAL fleet (one orchestrator per scope, by design) does not need. Wave E is its natural home.

Rival 2 — 'Pure client, zero server change': keep capacity a free-form string, encode JSON inside it, let route.py parse. Cheapest, no api/**. REJECTED: the string becomes a load-bearing secret protocol — vibes, not schema; the server can never validate; every future consumer (console tile, roster table) reads garbage; and the current silently-dropped-map behavior stays armed as a trap. It violates the wish's own words ('measured never vibes') and the PDF-D20 precedent that shared formulas get ONE validated home.

Winner — 'Structured facts from the server, the loop at the edges': minimal server change (validate + store structured capacity; keep beat/roster as the only verbs), measurement in the runner/skills, min(declared, observed) computed by route.py from server-provided facts (declared capacity + the observed task join the roster already ships), cap as an orchestrator-side spend ledger with the listener-side budget field as a second independent brake. Sharpest attack: the cap is orchestrator-local file state — a restart or second orchestrator could split spend truth, making the 'provable freeze' only as trustworthy as one file. Absorbed by: scoping honestly (one orchestrator per scope IS the design), making the ledger file deterministic + append-only + printed in the proof, and keeping TWO independent brakes (fleet cap at dispatch, per-listener budget in route.py) so a single stale file cannot un-brake the fleet. Second attack: the size-class threshold table is itself judgment — absorbed because the MEASUREMENT is real (sysctl/nproc) and declared stays a ceiling; the table is documented data anyone can audit. Third attack: parked skill listeners (TTL 900) read offline and the live router would starve them — absorbed by making pdf-bl-presence-honesty-sparse a named Decide ruling of THIS wave, fed by its own survey lane.

blocks.text: Survey digest (14 lanes returned — Digest, 2026-07-22)

content.value: ESTABLISHED. The direction survives survey contact with three corrections. (1) The server seam is exactly as small as hoped: beat_fields/1 (fleet.ex ~L251-259, origin/main) silently drops any non-string capacity — PROVEN LIVE by a raw POST against guerrilla (200 ok:true, field unchanged, no error) — and the fix is fully localized to that one function plus one :invalid_capacity controller arm; the roster read path passes maps through untouched, storage has no opinion, no test guards the drop. (2) The CLI dialect is settled by source + live probe: flags ALWAYS ride the query string (commandFlagBelongsInBody hardcodes cycle.open as the only body-routed command), flag types are documentation-only client-side, and a JSON-encoded-string --capacity already round-trips byte-identical today. Therefore the zero-Go path is forced: capacity stays a type:string flag carrying JSON text; the server accepts BOTH a native map (direct HTTP callers, free via Phoenix) AND a Jason-decoded JSON string (the CLI path — load-bearing, not optional) AND the legacy plain string (back-compat). (3) The spend meter is real for Claude (claude -p --output-format json emits total_cost_usd, verified 24/24 in METER.md + working code in run-cell.sh, with a native --max-budget-usd per-invocation brake), token-only for Codex (session rollout logs show token_count events, no dollar field — needs a rate table or honest token denomination), and absent for custom adapters (fall back to route.py's CLASS_COST with provenance tags: claude-cli-json | codex-token-rate | class-cost-fallback).

CORRECTIONS TO THE DIRECTION. First: the Strategize claim that 'the roster already ships the observed half — its read-time task join' is OVERSTATED. The task join (current_tasks_by_worker, Map.put_new) yields one busy/idle doc-id per worker — never a count, never a measurement; feeding today's actual roster rows into route.py was simulated and produced the EXACT INVERSE of the wave's proof (heavy unplaceable, light on the big box). min(declared, observed) exists NOWHERE and must originate at the edge: the listener self-clamps effective_class = min(observed-from-threshold-table, FLEET_MAX_CLASS) BEFORE beating, and the beat carries only the effective value — route.py needs no ceiling knowledge. Second: the egress leak is MORE severe than its backlog task claims. The webhook leg is inert (all 8 guerrilla hooks active:false and event-incompatible with 'create'), but journalctl on guerrilla shows a LIVE external SSE consumer (Go-http-client, ~15-20min reconnect cadence) on /w/default/p/default/v1/data/listen/production — the same workspace scope beat registrations land in, and forward_event?/replay_since filter workspace only, never type. Slice-now is confirmed on stronger grounds than PDF-D31's dissolution argument alone. Third: two naming seams are unreconciled and will silently break the proof at the glue if left to builders: the charter/brief say size_class, route.py says max_class (and the worker-protocol paper says max_size:'M' letter grades); last_seen is ISO8601 on the wire but route.py does float arithmetic — the glue MUST parse ISO to epoch or routing misbehaves quietly.

The glue is a NEW helpers/dispatch.sh — never a route.py --live mode (route.py's purity + 9-check selftest is the wave's most valuable iteration surface; the --route stdin JSON boundary already exists). file-order.sh already takes assignee as arg 3 — but it hardcodes its target via bp whoami, so the proof MUST inline curls (or patch env overrides) or it will file orders against PROD. The wish (verbatim core)

Wave B, the efficiency loop: (1) listeners MEASURE and advertise capacity in their beats — size class, slots free, budget state; measured never vibes, declared is a CEILING per PDF-D6. (2) The orchestrator skill + route.py consume the LIVE roster (min of declared and observed) so heavy->big and light->lean happens from real heartbeats, not static config. (3) The spend cap becomes a live brake: cap reached = ambition zero = dispatch halts, visibly and provably. (4) The proof-that-must-fire: a mixed batch routed against a live mixed-size roster lands heavy on the big listener and light on the lean one, driven by real beats — and with the cap tripped, dispatch provably freezes. Direction (tentative until Decide)

The finished experience: you run two listeners — one on the 32 GB box, one on a lean laptop — and each beat carries what the machine actually measured: its size class (derived from real RAM/cores, capped by the declared ceiling), its free slots, its remaining budget. The orchestrator types one dispatch command; the glue pulls the LIVE roster, computes min(declared, observed) from the server's own facts, and route.py lands the heavy export on the big box and the lint on the laptop — every decision printed with its reason. When the spend ledger crosses the cap, the next batch refuses loudly: every order listed as unplaceable with reason spend_cap, zero tasks filed, the freeze visible in one line. The direction debate

Rival 1 — 'The server owns efficiency': add /v1/fleet/route (or roster-computed effective capacity + a ledger-stored cap document). One authority, GUI-ready, multi-orchestrator-safe. REJECTED for this wave: it drags the whole loop behind the Elixir gate, hardens routing policy exactly when it should iterate fastest, edges toward a fifth verb, and buys distributed-truth machinery a PERSONAL fleet (one orchestrator per scope, by design) does not need. Wave E is its natural home.

Rival 2 — 'Pure client, zero server change': keep capacity a free-form string, encode JSON inside it, let route.py parse. Cheapest, no api/**. REJECTED: the string becomes a load-bearing secret protocol — vibes, not schema; the server can never validate; every future consumer (console tile, roster table) reads garbage; and the current silently-dropped-map behavior stays armed as a trap. It violates the wish's own words ('measured never vibes') and the PDF-D20 precedent that shared formulas get ONE validated home.

Winner — 'Structured facts from the server, the loop at the edges': minimal server change (validate + store structured capacity; keep beat/roster as the only verbs), measurement in the runner/skills, min(declared, observed) computed by route.py from server-provided facts (declared capacity + the observed task join the roster already ships), cap as an orchestrator-side spend ledger with the listener-side budget field as a second independent brake. Sharpest attack: the cap is orchestrator-local file state — a restart or second orchestrator could split spend truth, making the 'provable freeze' only as trustworthy as one file. Absorbed by: scoping honestly (one orchestrator per scope IS the design), making the ledger file deterministic + append-only + printed in the proof, and keeping TWO independent brakes (fleet cap at dispatch, per-listener budget in route.py) so a single stale file cannot un-brake the fleet. Second attack: the size-class threshold table is itself judgment — absorbed because the MEASUREMENT is real (sysctl/nproc) and declared stays a ceiling; the table is documented data anyone can audit. Third attack: parked skill listeners (TTL 900) read offline and the live router would starve them — absorbed by making pdf-bl-presence-honesty-sparse a named Decide ruling of THIS wave, fed by its own survey lane.
